title: Andromeda Galaxy
note: This is Andromeda galaxy and its satellite galaxy M110 (top of it). Took it on a real bright sky with full moon, so look out for a newer version.

title: North America Nebula
note: This is lower part of Cygnus and for reference the brightest star is Deneb in middle. This includes The Wall, North America Nebula (Right below Deneb), Sadr Region (Top left of Deneb, below Cygnus Star). You can also see some extra structures laying around which are part of the sab hill region.

title: Pleiades
note: This is Pleiades. One of the brightest star cluster in night sky and pretty much visible with naked eyes. Though you can not see the actual start structure from naked eyes, and that's the only reason why it is here.

title: Jupiter and moons
note: This is Jupiter with its 4 biggest moons; Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto. I took this through my phone from the eyepiece of a telescope, Celestron Powerseeker 70AZ. On the same day I saw Saturn as well, but wasnt lucky enough to take a photo.

title: Moon
note: I mean c'mon dude. This is literally moon. Everyone has taken pics of the moon once in their life. I just took it with a better camera.

title: Orion Nebula
note: One of my first target for deep sky photography. I have tones of photos of these but none of them are good enough. I learnt a lots of new things, its just I cant see it up in the sky right now and hence stay tuned until I come up with a fire pic of this nebula.

title: Comet C/2022 E3 (ZTF)
note: This was the commet that did a flyby of earth for the first time in 50000 YEARS. YES 50K. Its also called the 'Green commet' coming from Oort cloud. This is highly edited, but I was able to see the trail just like the image.

title: Lagoon Nebula
note: This image is from the Mt Abu in India. Single click photo covering Lagoon Nebula. This was part of a big image containing a lots of important points of the Milkyway. Will try this one more time, with better techniques and better software usage.

title: Ring Nebula
note: Was trying to get Vega the star, but ended up capturing a faint part of Ring Nebula, which I edited as per the nebula's color leading to a nice representation of the same. Btw this is about ~2570 ly.
